payload.body: A spectral-band feature is a quantitative descriptor computed from the per-bin energy values of a signal's power spectrum within a defined frequency sub-band [f_low, f_high), reducing the band-local energy vector to a scalar summary. The parameters are (1) the band bounds, (2) the underlying spectral decomposition, and (3) the specific scalar function applied (e.g., centroid, variance, flatness, flux). The construct persists as a standard computational routine implemented across audio analysis toolkits (Librosa, Essentia, HTK) and standardized in music information retrieval, speech processing, and acoustic monitoring systems. spectral-band-energy computes the total energy accumulated within a frequency band by summing the squared magnitude values |X[k]|² across all frequency bins in the band. This operation requires the per-bin energy values that constitute the spectral-band-distribution. Without the distribution — the ordered vector of per-bin energies — there are no individual values to sum. The dependency is operational: the distribution is the data object on which the summation that defines energy operates.
